method_notes: Bromley has no catchment areas and no community schools (all primaries are academies apart from two foundation schools, Edgebury and Poverest), so each school is its own admission authority. Primary Education in Bromley 2027-2028 booklet, 'Proximity, distance and all other children' (p.46): unless a school's arrangements say otherwise, distance is calculated in a straight line (as the crow flies) from the home address to the school using the Council's geographical information system (GIS), which uses the Council's gazetteer and Ordnance Survey address point data. The booklet does not specify the point at the school (gate/entrance/centroid) for the default; individual schools may define it (e.g. Southborough Primary: straight line to the main school gate). Some schools use random allocation within a criterion (booklet p.46). Coordinated scheme 2026/27 para 39: distance is from the child's permanent home address at the time of application. Distances in the booklet are in miles, as at the relevant national offer day.

gaps: All three years come from a single table in the 2027-28 booklet; not cross-checked against the 2026-27 booklet (its download URL now serves the newer booklet). 'N/A' is defined in the booklet as 'school undersubscribed, LA allocations made' and is recorded as all_offered. 'Church Criteria' recorded as no_distance_offers (last place went on a faith criterion; no distance printed). Orion Scotts Park appears in the directory (PAN 60) but not in the distances table, so it is marked not_published. Postcodes, PAN (2027 figures, not historical) and status come from the booklet directory, not cross-checked against GIAS. The booklet labels every non-foundation school 'Academy' and does not separate free schools (e.g. La Fontaine Academy and Langley Park Primary may be free schools); faith type inferred from school names. La Fontaine and Bickley Primary share the postcode BR1 2SQ (Nightingale Lane) in the booklet. Oddities as printed: Orion Mead Road (infant) 4.071 miles in 2026 vs about 1 mile before; Biggin Hill 3.440 (2024); Unicorn 3.932 and Pickhurst Infants 3.009 (2025); Langley Park shows N/A every year despite 236 applications for 30 places in 2026. The table gives only the furthest distance, not the criterion it was reached under. Academy/faith school measuring points not researched one by one; straight line assumed for all except where noted (Southborough, main gate). Junior schools (Alexandra, Crofton, Darrick Wood, Highfield Junior, Pickhurst Academy) excluded. Post-check: every 'N/A' was changed from all_offered to not_published. The booklet's footnote says N/A means undersubscribed, but it appears for oversubscribed schools too (e.g. Langley Park: 236 applications for 30 places; Tubbenden: 313 for 90), usually next to 'Information not available' in the appeals column.
